rules.sentence: The diagnosis of postpartum thyroiditis depends on clinical presentation and elevated free T4 and low thyroid-stimulating hormone.
Hyperthyroidism is transient and usually not treated.
Beta-blockers can be used if symptoms are present.
The American Thyroid Association recommends annual testing in women with hypothyroidism with a history of postpartum thyroiditis.[30]

This is a form of dilated cardiomyopathy that typically develops in the last month of pregnancy or within the first 5 months postpartum, characterized by left ventricular dysfunction without a preexisting heart condition.
Peripartum cardiomyopathy has symptoms similar to heart failure, and treatment follows the heart failure guidelines.
Prognosis varies; some mothers can have a full recovery, while others develop chronic heart failure.
For future pregnancies, women who developed Peripartum cardiomyopathy are at risk for recurrence.[31]
